title: Latency fingerprint sampler and regional graceful drain dashboard
creator: Aisha Kline
description:
Summary: We need a lightweight token-level latency fingerprint sampler and a paired dashboard that surfaces how graceful draining (regional node drain + capacity rebalancing) affects token SLIs and circuit-breaker tripping. This ticket covers the instrumentation, sampling algorithm, metric names, dashboard panels, and a rollout plan with a synthetic verification harness.

Background: Current token SLI dashboards show p50/p95/p99 rollups aggregated by region and path, but we lack a sampling signal that captures representative latency fingerprints for sequences when drains occur. During graceful drains we observe step increases in tail latency and correlated circuit-breaker admissions, but root attribution is noisy because of sampling bias and high-cardinality keys (tenant, model, path, seq_len).

Goals:
- Implement a deterministic sampler that captures a small, representative set of token-latency fingerprints per shard-region during high-risk events (node drain, autoscale down, rolling upgrade). Fingerprints include: request id, model, shard id, admitted path, sequence length bucket, KV cache hit flag, and per-token latencies for first 64 tokens (or until EOS).
- Expose a set of new metrics (counter + histogram + sampled traces) to correlate drains with SLO violations and circuit breaker transitions.
- Build a dashboard with panels for: fingerprint cadence, per-fingerprint token-latency waterfall, circuit-breaker state overlay, admission rate vs. token latency, and synthetic-run comparison.
- Instrument a short-term storage for sampled fingerprints (48h retention) and a retention policy that scrubs PII.

Acceptance criteria:
- New metrics emitted: rwi.fingerprint.emitted, rwi.fingerprint.latency_histogram (labels: region, shard, model, seq_len_bucket), rwi.fingerprint.kv_hit (gauge), and rwi.fingerprint.trace_ref (string tag to synthetic storage).
- Dashboard published in Grafana: 6 panels + links to sample details. Panels show live samples during a simulated drain and highlight circuit-breaker tripping.
- Synthetic harness (GH: redwood-infra/fingerprint-harness#42) reproduces a regional drain scenario and asserts p99 token latency delta < configured threshold for baseline customers; otherwise triggers a rollback plan.
- Sampling rate respects tenant budget and is disabled for flagged customers via config (tenant.allow_fingerprint=false).

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Deterministic sampling: use a hash of (request_id mod N) to pick samples to ensure reproducibility between runs and to avoid correlated bursts. N defaults to 1000; increase during experiments. We considered adaptive sampling by SLO risk, but opted for a fixed low-rate sampler to bound cost.
- Data volume: storing full per-token vectors is expensive. We store up to 64 token latencies and compress with delta-encoding before upload. Compression occurs at peer node and ingestion service stores compressed blob + metadata.
- Privacy: scrub prompt content and any user-supplied fields; only store metadata + per-token timing numbers. Include automated scrubber in ingestion pipeline.
- Circuit breaker signals: correlate fingerprint samples with circuit-breaker_open, circuit-breaker_attempted_fallback, and admission_reject_count. If a fingerprint co-occurs with a breaker_open event within 200ms window, mark sample with breaker=true.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrument runtime (serving) hot path to add sampler hook: node/runtime/sampler_v2.go (initial branch: feat/fingerprint-sampler).
2) Emit metrics via telemetry pipeline with labels: model, region, shard, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit. Metric naming follows conventions above.
3) Upload compressed fingerprint blobs to internal object store with prefix: s3://rwi-fingerprints/{region}/{date}/{shard}/{trace_ref}. Keep retention 48h initially.
4) Build Grafana panels and templated variables (region, model, shard, tenant). Dashboard link: grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency-fingerprints.
5) Create synthetic harness that performs controlled drains and validates metrics (GH PR: redwood-infra/fingerprint-harness#42).

Rollout & safety:
- Feature gated by runtime flag (runtime.enable_fingerprint_sampler). Default off in prod. Enable in staging then gradually enable in a small region.
- Disable for HIPAA/PCI tenants via tenant config.
- Unit tests covering compression/encoding and privacy scrubbing. Integration test in staging runs synthetic harness to validate no large increase in egress or latency.

Monitoring & runbook links:
- Playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Latency+Fingerprint+Sampler+Playbook
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd1234/latency-fingerprint-sampler
- Synthetic harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/fingerprint-harness/pull/42
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-example-design-doc

Next steps / open questions:
- Decide default sampling denominator (N=1000 by default). Ops: please advise on cost budget for samples per region.
- Confirm S3 retention and scrubbing SLA with security (48h vs 7 days).
- Add QA checklist for privacy verification before enabling on any customer data.

Estimated tasks:
- Runtime hook + sampler algorithm (Marco) - 3d
- Compression + ingest pipeline (Ravi) - 2d
- Grafana dashboard + templating (Priya) - 2d
- Synthetic harness + validation (QA) - 3d
- Rollout gating + tenant allowlist (Platform) - 1d

Point contacts: Aisha (owner), Marco (implementation), Priya (dashboard), Ravi (ingest), Nia (security review).
